w10_T4_005732: Liam had $19 saved in his piggy bank after doing chores that took him 120 minutes, or 2 hours, over the week. He spent $16 of it on a new comic book at the corner store. His grandmother then doubled whatever money he had left as a reward for his good grades. After that, the bus fare home cost him $1. Finally, he earned $45 walking dogs over the weekend, more than his friend Noah, who earned just $20 that week from his paper route. How much money did Liam have after walking the dogs?
w10_T4_005741: Mia started her sticker album with 14 stickers. At the school fair, a vendor was running a bonus round that made her collection five times as large as it had been. Then her teacher gave her 6 more stickers for finishing homework early, and a dozen classmates received the same reward. Next, a trading swap turned her whole collection into four times as many stickers as before. After the swap, she gave 40 stickers to her little sister, and then a second swap round made her stickers four times as many again. Finally, her aunt mailed her 80 more stickers. How many stickers did Mia end up with in her album?
w10_T4_005745: Ethan had 145 marbles in his jar. At a swap meet, three friends each brought exactly as many marbles as Ethan had and combined them with his, making his jar four times as full as before. He then traded away 276 marbles for a rare comic book, even though the vendor's stand had 60 different comic titles on display. Afterward, four more collectors each contributed a set exactly equal to what he had left, making his total five times as large. Finally, he donated 825 marbles to his school's collectors club. How many marbles did Ethan have left in his jar?
w10_T4_005746: Grandpa collected 167 eggs from the hen house early in the morning. By midday, the hens had laid 30 more eggs, which he added to the crate. In the afternoon, he sold 20 eggs to a neighbor. Later that afternoon, 10 more eggs turned up in a nest he'd missed. By evening, a second flock delivered 73 more eggs to the crate. How many eggs did Grandpa have in the crate by evening?
w10_T4_005749: Sophie started her lemonade stand with $42 in the cash box, which is 4200 cents. During a summer fair, first five nearby stands and then eight more identical stalls each pooled in an amount equal to what she currently had, growing her cash box to five times, and then eight times, its size. Unfortunately, she had to pay $1,451 to replace a broken cooler and canopy. A generous donor then added $73 to the box. The fair organizers split the remaining shared fund evenly between her stand and one partner stand, so she kept half. Finally, she paid $94 in rent for the stall space. How much money did Sophie end up with?
w10_T4_005760: Ms. Ada had 108 books on the returns shelf at the start of the day, even though the library has a dozen reading rooms in total. She then checked in 64 more books that students had returned overnight. Next, she pulled 97 books to send back to the district office. A book fair donated four identical extra crates, each holding as many books as were already on the shelf, making the shelf's count five times as large. The librarian then split that total evenly across 3 storage shelves and kept only the books on one shelf. Finally, a donation event brought in enough books to make that shelf's count nine times as large. How many books were on Ms. Ada's shelf after the donation event?
w10_T4_005765: Jason had 116 baseball cards in his binder. He traded away 2 cards for a rare rookie card. At a card show, eight other collectors each brought a set exactly equal to what Jason had, and they combined collections, making Jason's share nine times as large, even though the show had 300 vendors set up that day. He then had to give up 403 cards to pay off a bet he lost. Finally, he won 48 more cards in a raffle, ending up with far more than his friend Marcus, who only had 90 cards. How many cards did Jason have at the end?
w10_T4_005774: Farmer Dale picked 173 tomatoes from his garden on Monday, in a garden that spans 12 rows total. On Tuesday he picked 15 more. A raccoon got into the shed and ruined 130 of them overnight. On Wednesday he found 3 tomatoes he'd missed the first time. He then gave 32 tomatoes to his neighbor. Finally, he picked 53 more on Thursday. How many tomatoes did Farmer Dale have by Thursday?
w10_T4_005776: Chef Nora baked 151 muffins before dawn, a batch that took 240 minutes, or 4 hours, in the oven rotation. A catering order came in for four times as many muffins as she already had, so she quadrupled her batch by baking three more identical rounds, even though her kitchen has a dozen ovens in total. She then added 42 muffins for a school fundraiser. Later she baked 75 more for a wedding order. Finally, she added 17 more muffins for a walk-in customer. How many muffins did Chef Nora end up with?
w10_T4_005779: Zoe had 81 coins in her video game account, which she had earned over 180 minutes, or 3 hours, of play. She then found a treasure chest worth 63 more coins. In the end she had far more than her rival Kayla, who only finished with 500 coins. How many coins did Zoe have after the boss battle?
w10_T4_005782: In the morning, Mr. Kim counted 119 fish in his display tank, out of the 30 tanks in his shop. By midday, 72 fish had been sold to customers. In the afternoon, he added 29 new fish from a delivery. A wholesaler then offered a deal where three tanks just like his were combined, tripling his fish count. Later that afternoon, 67 more fish arrived from a rescue shelter. By evening, a final delivery made his total six times as large. How many fish did Mr. Kim have in his tank by evening?
w10_T4_005789: Uncle Theo had 103 rare coins in his collection. He sold 74 of them to a dealer to pay for a trip. He then traded away 19 more coins for a single gold coin he wanted. A collectors' club event let six members each add a set equal to his remaining coins, making his total six times as large. A second club chapter did the same with seven equal sets, making it seven times as large again. A national convention then repeated the six-way pooling, and finally a seven-way pooling closed out the event. How many coins did Uncle Theo end up with?
w10_T4_005794: In the morning, the community center collected 87 aluminum cans for recycling, a job that took 60 minutes, or 1 hour, to sort. By midday, 12 more cans came in from a neighborhood drop-off. A school recycling drive then pooled in four more batches exactly equal in size, making the total five times as large. In the afternoon, 38 more cans arrived from the local diner. By evening, a final citywide drive made the can count eight times as large. How many cans did the community center end up with by evening?
w10_T4_005804: Sam packed 68 apples for a group hiking trip. Along the trail, 52 more apples were added from a farm stand they passed. At base camp, three other hiking groups combined their apple supplies equally with Sam's, making the total four times as large. That evening, 38 more apples were donated by a passing trail crew. Finally, 40 more apples arrived with the last group to reach camp. How many apples were in the group's supply by the end?
w10_T4_005812: The chess club's point tally started the season at 141 points. After the first tournament, the team earned 76 more points. A tough away match then cost them 98 points. The following week, a scoring error was found and 82 points were deducted. A forfeited match then cost the team 28 more points. A season-ending bonus round made the team's final tally nine times as large. How many points did the chess club end the season with?
w10_T4_005819: Priya's bike shop had 218 bikes in stock at the start of the month. A small supplier delivered 6 more bikes. She then sold 58 bikes during a weekend promotion. A big shipment brought in 80 more bikes. A merger with a partner store, matching her stock exactly, doubled her total inventory. A second matching shipment then doubled it again. By month's end she had far more bikes than her rival Diego, whose shop only held 300 bikes. How many bikes did Priya's shop have at the end of the month?
w10_T4_005820: Wendy filled a candy jar with 128 pieces of candy for a party, worth 12,800 cents in total value at the store's pricing. She added 23 more pieces from a bulk bag. A second bag added 56 more pieces. A latecomer guest brought 16 more pieces to contribute. A candy exchange with two other party tables, each matching the jar's count, made the jar's total three times as large. Finally, 16 more pieces were added from the leftover party favors. How many pieces of candy were in the jar at the end?
w10_T4_005821: In the morning, Owen had 72 comic books in his collection, stored across 9 different boxes. By midday, he bought 17 more issues at a yard sale. In the afternoon, two friends each contributed a stack exactly equal to his, making his collection three times as large. Later that afternoon, he sold 40 comics to a used bookstore. By evening, he traded away 167 comics for a single rare first edition. How many comic books did Owen have left by evening?
w10_T4_005823: In the morning, the toy store had 113 toy cars on display. A delivery truck doubled that number by dropping off an identical matching shipment. By midday, a second matching shipment made the display's count four times as large. In the afternoon, 38 cars were sold to customers. That evening, a return shipment added 47 more cars. Finally, a closing sale event made the display's count seven times as large. How many toy cars were on display at the end?
w10_T4_005825: The camp had 202 logs stacked for the bonfire, even though a dozen campers had signed up for the trip. Rain ruined 32 logs overnight. The next day, a supply truck delivered 32 replacement logs. A local farmer then donated 18 more logs. Finally, 111 logs were used for the closing night bonfire. How many logs were left in the camp's stack?
w10_T4_005831: In the morning, Mai had 29 roses ready at her flower shop, out of a dozen varieties she stocks. By midday, a delivery brought in 72 more roses. In the afternoon, five other florists pooled in matching batches, making her total six times as large. That evening, 341 roses were sold for a big wedding order. Later that night, 40 more roses arrived from a late supplier. Finally, a bulk order matched seven times over, making her total eight times as large before closing. How many roses did Mai have at closing?
w10_T4_005835: In the morning, Ravi's bookstore had 162 novels on the shelf, arranged across a dozen genres. In the afternoon, 72 more books arrived from a returning book club. Later, 19 more books were donated by a local author. How many books were on display at closing?
w10_T4_005836: The pet shop started the day with 118 goldfish in the display tank, after a 180-minute, or 3-hour, water treatment cycle. A supplier delivered 63 more fish. A breeding program made the tank's count seven times as large. Finally, 121 fish were sold during a weekend sale. How many goldfish were left in the tank?
w10_T4_005838: Emma had $133 in her savings account. She deposited $19 from her allowance. Then she added $53 from a birthday gift. She withdrew $132 to buy a new phone. A bank fee took another $29. She then paid $5 for a subscription renewal. Finally, she deposited $38 from babysitting, ending with more than her brother Leo, who had only $50 saved. How much money did Emma have in her account at the end?
w10_T4_005846: Ms. Liu had 115 colored pencils in her classroom bin, stored in a cabinet with a dozen empty drawers. She ordered 33 more pencils for a new unit. During inventory, she discovered 123 pencils were missing or broken and had to discard them, even though the school has 20 art classrooms in total. A donation drive then brought in 66 more pencils. Finally, a supply closet clean-out added 54 more pencils to the bin. How many pencils did Ms. Liu have in the bin at the end?
